title: Warsh's First FOMC Holds Rate at 3.50–3.75%; Hawkish Dot Plot Shows Median Hike, Not Cut
detail: The FOMC under new Chair Kevin Warsh unanimously held the federal funds rate at 3.50-3.75% in his first meeting as Chair. The accompanying Summary of Economic Projections turned notably hawkish: the 2026 median dot rose to 3.8% from 3.4% in the March projections — implying a hike rather than a cut — with 9 of 18 members projecting at least one 2026 hike (6 of those projecting two or more). The Committee's 2026 PCE inflation forecast was raised to 3.6% from 2.7%. Warsh declined to submit his own dot, telling reporters he found the tool 'inconsistent with his views' on communicating policy intentions. The post-meeting statement was cut to roughly 130 words, down from 341 words in April — a marked change in Fed communication style under the new chair.

title: US-Iran MOU Formally Signed — Strait of Hormuz Reopens, Brent Crashes ~11%
detail: The US-Iran memorandum of understanding was formally signed and entered into force: Iran agreed to immediately reopen the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping, and the US agreed to lift its naval blockade of Iranian ports. The MOU sets up 60 days of follow-on talks toward a permanent peace deal. Oil prices collapsed on the news — Brent crude fell as much as 11% to roughly $96/barrel, WTI fell roughly 14% to about $96 — while Asian equity markets hit fresh records (Nikkei, Kospi, and Taiex all posted gains). The 10-year Treasury yield fell 9bp to 4.25% as rate-hike odds eased on the improved energy-price outlook, partially offsetting the hawkish signal from the same-day Warsh dot plot.
